animator.ablauf.reise: One after another — with a cinematic flight between legs. Chosen in the archive.
animator.ablauf.schwarm: Simultaneous (swarm) — the longest tour sets the video length. Chosen in the archive.
animator.alpha.hint: Output is a .mov (ProRes 4444) — larger than MP4 but NLE-ready (Premiere/Final Cut/DaVinci). Map style, terrain, pitch and codec are ignored in this mode.
animator.alpha.preview_hint: Alpha mode active — the map will not be in the final video.
animator.alpha.tooltip: Renders only the track + overlays on a transparent background. Output is a ProRes-4444 .mov file that can be dropped directly over real footage in Premiere/Final Cut/DaVinci.
animator.alpha_multi: “No map (alpha)” currently works with a single tour only — please remove the extra tours or pick a map style.
animator.btn.save_defaults: Keep this look for new tracks
animator.btn.save_defaults_tip: Resolution, map style, overlays, colours etc. of this track become the default for all NEW tracks (same as Settings → Defaults). Existing tracks stay unchanged.
animator.charts.adopt_default: Default style applied (nothing set in the Data Animator yet).
animator.charts.adopt_none: Nothing set in the Data Animator yet — keeping the default style.
animator.charts.adopt_ok: Style adopted from the Data Animator.
animator.charts.empty_nogpx: Load a track first, then add charts.
animator.charts.help: Overlay fully styled data charts (elevation, heart rate, speed …) onto the video. Design the look in the Data Animator and adopt it here. Stays in sync with the dot on the map.
animator.charts.title: Charts
animator.codec.prores_hint: Studio quality for video editing — output is .mov, several hundred MB per render.
animator.colors.hint: The first colour applies from km 0 (= track colour). Each entry sets a new colour from its km on.
animator.colors.hint_metric: Each entry sets a new colour from its value on. “Auto” fills min→max. “hard” = bands, “gradient” = smooth transition.
animator.colors.no_metric: No data available for this source.
animator.colors.tooltip: Lets the track change colour — by distance or by any data series the track provides (elevation, speed, gradient, heart rate, power, cadence, temperature …). The change is either hard or a smooth gradient.
animator.dot.smooth_hint: To the left the arrow follows every twitch, to the right it shows the general direction. In brackets: how much track around the point the direction is read from.
animator.dur.keine_zeiten: This track has no timestamps — real-time mode not possible.
animator.field.camera_follow_track_toolt: When on, the camera re-centers on the current track point each frame. Off: camera stays locked to the configured map position.
animator.field.cinematic_flyto_tooltip: On large zoom jumps (globe→detail), the camera takes a slightly arcing path — like Mapbox' flyTo. Nice cinematic effect, but can feel 'zooms out too far'. Disable for strict linear interpolation.
animator.field.ortho_tip: Affects only the official aerial imagery (not the base layer) — same in preview, video and web map.
animator.field.mapadj_tip: Affects the map, not the track or overlays — same in preview and video. Vector maps: brightness only.
animator.field.stars_tip: The sky behind the globe — visible once the camera is far enough out. Same in preview and video.
animator.field.follow_height_tip: Stops the camera from bobbing up and down over mountainous terrain. 0 = camera follows the ground, 100 = fixed cruising height (stays level no matter the terrain).
animator.field.follow_inertia_tip: 0 = locked to the point (can jitter), higher = the camera trails more smoothly
animator.field.padding_tip: Space between the track and the image edge
animator.field.smooth_camera_tip: Stops the camera bobbing up and down over mountainous 3D terrain. Off = classic (default). On = smooth, decoupled camera.
animator.field.spin_tooltip: Constant rotation speed (degrees per second). Works everywhere — intro, animation and hold. Positive = clockwise, negative = counter-clockwise. On globe view: Earth rotates.
animator.field.static_pins_tip: Show start and end point as markers on the map
animator.fokus.label: Camera follows
animator.ghost.tooltip: Ghost track: draws the whole route faintly/semi-transparent in the background while only the animated portion is drawn fully opaque on top. Handy to see where the route still goes.
animator.glow.tooltip: Colored aura/halo around the track. Makes it pop against the map. Off or 0 — just the bare line. Strength controls how soft the halo is.
animator.haupt_start.hint: It waits, then runs faster and catches up by the end of the video — preview and video show the same thing.
animator.haupt_start.label: Main tour starts after
animator.help.label.kf_delete: How do I delete a keyframe?
animator.hide_labels.tooltip: Hides all text and icons on the map — place names, road names, POI labels. Turns the map into a clean background. Looks particularly tidy in outdoor-style animations.
animator.karte_fehler: The map could not be loaded (Mapbox token or style):
animator.kf.alt_zoom: {n} zoom keyframes come from an older version. The zoom in the video may differ from the preview — best to set those keyframes again.
animator.kf.center_tooltip: Map position of this keyframe. Longitude is unwrapped: values beyond ±180° = full earth turns on the way from the previous keyframe (like Insta360). Dragging the map counts the value up automatically.
animator.kf.copied: Keyframe copied — press ⌘V to paste at the playhead
animator.kf.deactivate_warn_body: You have keyframes set. Disabling the keyframe editor now will delete all keyframes and bring back classic camera control. Continue?
animator.kf.delete_hint: Quick-delete: right-click the marker in the bar (or the pin on the map) · <kbd>Del</kbd> key when the keyframe is selected.
animator.kf.empty_hint: No keyframe selected yet. Set up the map (pan + tilt) however you want, then click "📍 Drop keyframe here" under the map — or click an existing 🎥 marker.
animator.kf.enable_hint: Turn this on to drive the camera animation with track-position-based keyframes. Otherwise the animation runs classically with static tilt + steady rotation.
animator.kf.enable_tooltip: Enables the camera-keyframe timeline for cinematic camera moves. Off: classic behaviour with static pitch + linear rotation sweep.
animator.kf.follow_hint_free: Free map view — the map stays where you panned it.
animator.kf.follow_hint_track: Camera follows the GPS point — panning is ignored. Pitch/bearing/zoom stay individual per keyframe.
animator.kf.follow_tip: On: camera stays at the GPS point of the anchor — pitch/bearing/zoom still set individually. Off: free map view (panning the map sticks).
animator.kf.hint: Tip: drag, rotate, tilt the map — then click „Update with current map view" above. Or use the sliders to fine-tune.
animator.kf.pitch_reset_tip: Reset pitch to 0° (needed for globe/world view — otherwise the map is tilted and the globe appears off-center).
animator.kf.position_tooltip: Framing: shifts the whole earth view WITHIN the picture — X horizontally, Y vertically, -50% to +50% of the frame. The camera stays put, only the picture slides.
animator.kf.rotation_tooltip: World rotation around the polar axis for this keyframe. -180° to +180°. Two KFs with different values rotate the earth between them.
animator.kf.spin_tooltip: Rotation speed (degrees per second) from this keyframe. Linearly interpolated to the next KF. 0 = no spin. Positive = clockwise.
animator.kf.world_center_bbox_tip: Globe view centered on the WORLD CENTER (Greenwich/Equator). Classic front-on Earth view like before — the track sits off-center and the camera flies into it on render. In KF mode creates a world KF.
animator.kf.world_center_start_tip: Globe view centered on the track START POINT. When zooming in, the start point stays fixed — the earth rotates around it without wandering laterally through the world. In KF mode creates a world KF.
animator.kf.world_center_tooltip: Center the map on the globe view (pitch=0, zoom=1.5, track midpoint). In KF mode this also creates a world KF at the current scrubber anchor.
animator.kf.world_drag_hint: 🌍 Earth sitting too low? Just drag it up with your mouse — the keyframe updates automatically when you release.
animator.lane.center_tip: Earth point: which point of the earth sits under the camera. Changing it ROTATES the earth under the camera (values beyond ±180° = full turns).
animator.lane.cluster_tip: Click: select all properties · Drag: move them together · Right-click: delete the entire cluster
animator.lane.position_tip: Framing: shifts the earth view within the picture (±50%). The camera stays put — only the picture slides, e.g. to make room for text.
animator.line_style_spacing.tooltip: Multiplies the dash/dot length in the line pattern. Only active for Dashed/Dotted/Dash-Dot.
animator.map_config.tooltip: Lighting, labels, boundaries — everything Mapbox lets us configure.
animator.open_tourmap.tip: Switches to the Tour-Map and takes over the exact current view/zoom/rotation — exportable there as PNG or interactive HTML.
animator.osm_only: In OSM mode only one map style is available. Add a Mapbox token for satellite & 3D.
animator.overlay.entry_hint: How the stats boxes appear in the video. Only visible in the rendered video / probe run.
animator.overlay.show_pretrim_tip: When active: track line is drawn from the start of the track (pre-trim portion visible as background). When off: line starts at the left trim-handle.
animator.overlay.stats_use_trim_tip: When active: Stats overlay shows values for the render trim range (distance, elevation, time only for the trimmed section). Otherwise: always the full-track values.
animator.overlay.timing_tip: Show this box only within this time window (video seconds). Empty / 0 = from start resp. until end.
animator.pace.even_desc: The dot moves at a steady pace along the route.
animator.pace.raw_desc: Follows your device's own rhythm (as before).
animator.pace.real_desc: The dot is fast where you were fast.
animator.pace.wirkung: Effect on this tour: the run shifts by up to {p} % compared to “even”.
animator.pace.wirkung_min: This tour was recorded so evenly that this distribution is barely visible (at most {p} % shift).
animator.pace_mode.hint: This decides how the dot is spread along the route — not how long the video runs (that is the duration). “Even” looks calm and always works. “Real pace” needs timestamps and shows where you ran and where you dawdled; planned routes have none, which is why it is greyed out. “As recorded” follows whatever your device stored — which is unpredictable (one measured file had 1121 metres between two points) and is only there so older projects still look the way they did.
animator.pause.info: Your tour: {gesamt}, of which {steh} standing still in {n} stops.
animator.pause.none: No stops above the threshold on this tour.
animator.pause.result_show: About {voll} of the video will stand still.
animator.pause.result_trim: Untreated the video would stand still for about {voll}; with this setting it is {jetzt}.
animator.playwright_missing.body: The Animator uses a headless Chromium browser to render the 3D Mapbox map for every frame. This browser has not been downloaded yet.
animator.playwright_missing.body2: One-time download (~150 MB). After that rendering works out-of-the-box. Stored in the system cache at:
animator.playwright_missing.installing: Downloading browser (~150 MB, this may take a moment) …
animator.playwright_missing.title: Render browser missing
animator.point_count.hint: Default is all points from your GPX. Drag the slider left to make the track coarser — the preview updates live. Affects render: fewer points = slightly faster. Render time depends mostly on duration × FPS × resolution. Note: the trial run still shows the full point density — the reduction applies to the rendered video (and the still preview of the line).
animator.progress.ffmpeg: ffmpeg finalising (+faststart, may take a moment) …
animator.progress.ruhig_nur_mapbox: Smooth camera (3D) is only available with Mapbox styles — using the classic camera.
animator.render_error.body: An error occurred during rendering. See traceback and log file below for details.
animator.render_error.title: Render failed
animator.render_needs_token.body: Animator render is not available in OSM mode (no satellite, no 3D terrain). Add a free Mapbox token in settings.
animator.render_needs_token.title: Render needs a Mapbox token
animator.rotcounter.tooltip: Live rotation counter: shows the unwrapped longitude and the number of full earth turns while you drag the map.
animator.schwarm_dezent: Don't highlight the main tour (blend in)
animator.schwarm_form: Use the main tour's runner shape for all tours (e.g. arrow)
animator.shadow.dir_tooltip: Global light direction for the drop shadow — applies to the track AND all signs. 0° = right, 90° = down, 180° = left, 270° = up.
animator.shadow.tooltip: Makes the track look like a line floating above the map. With 3D terrain the shadow stays on the ground while the track is rendered 150 m above — gives a 3D look.
animator.snapshot.tip: Renders exactly the frame currently shown in the preview (partial track, camera, overlays) as a full-resolution image.
animator.stats.empty_hint: Load a GPX file — track stats will appear here
animator.style.alpha_hint: Renders only the track + overlays on a transparent background. Output is a .mov file (ProRes 4444) that can be dropped directly over real footage in Premiere/Final Cut/DaVinci. Map style, 3D terrain and lighting have no effect in this mode.
animator.style.osm_disabled_body: Without a Mapbox token only the OSM default map is available — no satellite, no 3D terrain, no style switching. Rendering is disabled as well.
animator.style.osm_disabled_body_static: Without a Mapbox token the OSM default map is used — no satellite, no 3D terrain, no style switching. PNG rendering still works (with the OSM map).
animator.timeline.anim_end_tip: End of the track animation, start of the hold phase. Keyframes to the right of this line move the camera while the track endpoint stays put.
animator.timeline.anim_start_tip: End of the intro phase, start of the track animation. Keyframes to the left of this line move the camera before the track starts moving.
animator.timeline.clear_tip: Removes all camera keyframes. The Pitch/Rotation sliders become active again afterwards.
animator.timeline.cluster.tip: Click: select all properties · Drag: move them together · Right-click: delete the entire cluster
animator.timeline.dblclick_hint: Double-click on a lane (Pitch / Rotation / Zoom / Position) sets just that one property at the click position — no full cluster. Handy when you only want to animate bearing, for instance. Double-clicking the Cluster row at the top sets all 4 together as usual.
animator.timeline.easing.title: Transition to next keyframe
animator.timeline.fulltrack_tip: On: the full track stays visible in the preview (no trim to scrubber position). Off: track is trimmed up to the scrubber — same as the final render.
animator.timeline.gesture_hint: 💡 Tip: drag the map normally — <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+Drag (Mac) or right-click+Drag tilts it. Then click „Capture keyframe".
animator.timeline.kfpins_tip: On: keyframe pins (yellow dots on the map) visible — editing aid. Off: WYSIWYG mode, pins won't appear in the final render anyway.
animator.timeline.marker.tip: Click: select + edit · Right-click: delete · Drag: move
animator.timeline.play_tip: Plays the animation once at the configured duration — quick preview without rendering. Press again (or Space) to stop.
animator.timeline.smooth.label: Smooth camera in this section
animator.timeline.smooth.tip: Smooths the camera's up-and-down over the terrain in this section only. The “Smooth camera” box in the sidebar applies to the whole video.
animator.timeline.snap_tip: Snapshots the current map view (pitch / bearing / zoom) as a new keyframe at the scrubber position.
animator.timeline.trim_end_tip: Drag render end — determines where the render finishes.
animator.timeline.trim_start_tip: Drag render start — determines where the render begins. KFs before this point are used as run-up motion.
animator.timeline.zoom.tip: Timeline zoom: Ctrl/Cmd + Mousewheel · +/− buttons · Click number to reset to 1×. At zoom > 1: Shift+Wheel pans, Shift+Drag moves the visible range.
animator.tours.hint: Additional tours are animated after the first one — the camera flies cinematically from one to the next.
animator.tours.lade_abgebrochen: Loading cancelled — your selection is still in the library.
animator.tours.lade_warte: Please wait — the preview with all tours will build right after.
animator.tours.missing: Some saved tours could not be found.
animator.tours.missing_n: {n} saved tour(s) could not be found — see the log for details.
animator.tours.start_delay: Starts after … seconds of video time (0 = starts together)
animator.video_load_fail: Preview could not load — use “▶ Play” for the system player.
animator.wm.drag_hint: Drag the logo in the preview to wherever it should sit.
animator.wm.title: Watermark
animator.wm.zurueck: Back to the GPS Studio logo

bib.belegt_text: Another GPS Studio instance has this library open. Two at once would overwrite each other's data.
bib.cloud_abgelehnt: This folder belongs to {dienst}, so it cannot be used.
bib.cloud_hinweis: Cloud folders such as Dropbox, iCloud Drive or OneDrive will not work: they swap files out mid-write, which corrupts the database. External drives and NAS are fine.
bib.defekt_text: Your library's database cannot be read. Your track files are not affected — only the index. You can restore a backup; the damaged file is set aside, not deleted.
bib.fehlt_beruhigung: Nothing was deleted and nothing new was created. Your data is still where it was.
bib.fehlt_text: GPS Studio cannot find your library right now. If it lives on an external drive or a network share, connect it and search again.
bib.g_db_unlesbar: The copied database could not be read — your existing data stays put.
bib.g_eltern_fehlt: The parent folder does not exist.
bib.g_kein_schreibrecht: GPS Studio is not allowed to write there.
bib.g_kopie_unvollstaendig: The copy was incomplete — nothing was changed.
bib.g_nicht_wegraeumbar: The old folder could not be tidied away.
bib.g_sicherung_unmoeglich: No backup could be created, so the move was aborted.
bib.g_ziel_nicht_leer: The target folder is not empty.
bib.keine_sicherung: There is no backup. Please get in touch before deleting anything.
bib.nicht_leer: That folder is not empty. GPS Studio will create its own subfolders there — better to pick a folder of its own.
bib.nicht_offen: The library is not open right now.
bib.umzug_fehler_text: GPS Studio tried to move your existing data into a library and stopped. Nothing was deleted — your existing data is untouched where it was.
bib.umzug_lauf_text: GPS Studio sets up a library once and copies your collection into it. Nothing is deleted — the old location is only renamed. If your tours live on a network drive this can take a few minutes.
bib.umzug_ok_alt: The old data was not deleted, only renamed — if anything is missing, it is still there.
bib.umzug_ok_ort: You are free to choose this location. If you would rather keep your tours on an external drive or a network share, you can move the library right here — GPS Studio really moves it, it does not start over.
bib.umzug_ok_spaeter: Later you will find this under Settings → Library → „Move to another location …“. This report is available there again, too.
bib.umzug_ok_text: GPS Studio now keeps tours and projects in a library. Everything you had has moved there in full.
bib.willkommen_text: Your tours, projects and settings live in a library — a folder you choose yourself. You can move it later at any time.
bugreport.dau.hint: Easiest way: click '📄 Save log to Desktop' — a file lands on your desktop that you can simply drag into your email to Marc. This guarantees the full log gets attached.
bugreport.desktop_fail: Could not save the log to the desktop.
bugreport.desktop_ok: Done! '{name}' is now on your desktop — just drag the file into your email to Marc.
bugreport.hint: The body contains a placeholder '[hier deinen Text einfügen]' — please replace it with a short description of what you were doing. You don't need to understand the log excerpt; it helps Marc debug.
bugreport.immer_mit: The log is written continuously — you do not need to wait for an error message. Just send it after something did not work as expected.
bugreport.intro: Copy the address + text and paste it into your mail program or webmail (Gmail/Outlook/…). If you have a local mail program installed, you can also use '📧 Open mail app'.
bugreport.label.subject: Subject
bugreport.title: Feedback / Bug report to Marc
cloud.anl_s1: Click the button below — the app puts the file rz-cloud.php on your desktop.
cloud.anl_s2: Upload this file into a folder of your web space (e.g. “archive”) — with your FTP program or your host’s file manager. Your web space only needs PHP and HTTPS; virtually every host can do that.
cloud.anl_s3: Enter the web address of that file below (https://yoursite.com/archive/rz-cloud.php) and click “Create new archive”.
cloud.anl_s4: The app will then show your password and access key ONCE. Save both in your password manager — without the password nobody can open the archive, not even us.
cloud.anl_titel: How to set it up (once, about 5 minutes)
cloud.aus_hinweis: Set up your cloud archive — click for the guide
cloud.auto_bereit: Automatic sync: ready — uploads by itself after changes
cloud.auto_wartet: Automatic sync: changes detected, starting shortly
cloud.daten_hinweis: Together with your archive passphrase this gets you to the archive from any computer. The passphrase itself cannot be shown again — it lives only in your password manager.
cloud.entfernen_tip: Remove from the cloud (goes to the trash)
cloud.fehlt: Parts needed for the cloud are missing (cryptography, keyring). Please reinstall the app.
cloud.gefunden_belegt: There is already an archive there.
cloud.herunterladen_hinweis: Fetches everything missing here — for a second computer or after data loss. Existing files are not overwritten.
cloud.intro: Your archive lives on your own web server — encrypted. Upload the file rz-cloud.php into a folder of your web space and enter that file's address here.
cloud.intro2: Your tour archive, encrypted on your own web space: if this computer dies, everything is still there — and a second computer can connect to the same archive.
cloud.korb_alt_hinweis: {n} entries come from an older version of the cloud archive — their names can no longer be read. They are not needed any more and disappear by themselves after 30 days.
cloud.menge_schon_da: This composition already exists here — local work stays.
cloud.menge_tour_fehler: One tour could not be imported
cloud.menge_touren_fehlen: Not all tours of this composition are available.
cloud.nicht_eingerichtet: The cloud is not set up.
cloud.nur_https: Only https:// is allowed — over http:// the access key would travel unencrypted.
cloud.optional: This is optional. Without a cloud the app works exactly as before and everything stays local.
cloud.passwort_hinweis: Save it in your password manager now. You need it to connect a second computer. If it is lost, nobody can reach the data any more — not even us.
cloud.php_fehler: That didn’t work — see the log.
cloud.php_fehlt: The server file is missing from this installation.
cloud.schluesselbund_zu: The keychain denied access. Cloud sync is paused; any cloud action in the dialog will try again.
cloud.schon_da: There is already an archive there. Use “Connect to an existing one” and your passphrase.
cloud.stillgelegt: The cloud archive is paused while the tour library is being rebuilt. Anything you already uploaded stays untouched — the cloud will come back afterwards.
cloud.tour_fehlt: This tour is not (or no longer) in the archive.
cloud.trennen_hinweis: This computer will forget the access and data key. Note your access key first — without it and your passphrase you cannot get back into the archive:
cloud.trennen_nochmal: Click the button once more to disconnect.
cloud.zugang_unvollstaendig: Access data in the keychain is incomplete — please disconnect in the cloud dialog and connect again.

first_run.intro: You have two options for the maps in this app:
first_run.intro2: Maps and satellite imagery come without any sign-up: free aerial imagery from national mapping agencies (Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Spain, France and more), OpenStreetMap maps and 3D terrain. Videos rendered with them may be published on YouTube etc. — the source attribution is placed in the picture automatically.
first_run.keys_desc: MapTiler (satellite worldwide, videos allowed up to 100,000 subscribers) and Mapbox (videos only with purchased rights) can be added any time under Settings → Map providers.
first_run.keys_title: More styles with your own key (optional)
first_run.opt_osm_can: Ready without a token: 📷 geotag photos · 🗺️ tour map as image · 🧭 clean up tracks · 📈 elevation-profile videos.
first_run.opt_osm_desc: Works instantly, no account. But only basic map (no satellite, no 3D, no animator render).
first_run.opt_token_desc: Satellite, 3D terrain, premium styles, hi-res renders. Free Mapbox account in 2 min.
first_run.title: Welcome — set up your maps
first_run.title2: Welcome — you can start right away
first_run.token_what: A “token” is a free access key for the premium maps (satellite, 3D). Optional — you can also add it later in Settings.
geotagger.addr.hint: This address is written into the photo when tagging (IPTC/XMP). All fields empty = no address.
geotagger.autotag.title: Image recognition running …
geotagger.badge.notime: No usable capture time (EXIF) — cannot be matched

gpxinspect.fillmode_tip: How gaps are filled: 'Straight line' interpolates directly (fast). 'Walking/Cycling/Car' finds the real route on the path/road network for each gap (Mapbox, needs internet + token) — looks much more natural with many gaps. Very large gaps (e.g. flights) are filled linearly automatically.
gpxinspect.heal_done_route: Healed: %s spikes · %r gaps snapped to route, %l filled straight
gpxinspect.heal_help: Automatically finds and fixes GPS outliers and gaps. Pick scope and actions, then Heal. Undo anytime.
gpxinspect.heal_need_ab: Scope 'Section A→B': set two points on the map first (A green, B red).
gpxinspect.heal_nothing_sel: Nothing selected — tick what should be healed.
gpxinspect.heal_opt_routegaps: Snap gaps to real paths/roads (otherwise straight line)
gpxinspect.heal_opt_tempo_help: Some GPS jumps are a permanent offset: the track leaps e.g. 40 m and stays there — smoothing positions cannot heal that, because the distance really was covered; only the timestamps claim “in 3 seconds”. This option corrects the TIME of such spots to the usual pace of the surroundings. The tour gets a few seconds longer; distance and positions stay untouched.
gpxinspect.heal_run_hint: 'Snap to paths' finds the real route (Mapbox, needs internet + token). Very large gaps (e.g. flights) stay straight. Undo anytime.
gpxinspect.heal_tip: Place the points between A and B onto the straight line (position + elevation interpolated). Timestamps stay → speed becomes realistic again.
gpxinspect.healed: Segment smoothed — time kept, speed corrected.
gpxinspect.help: Click two points on the map one after another (anchor A green, B red). Then pick an action for the segment in between.
gpxinspect.help_auto: Heal gaps and outliers automatically: tick what should happen, then press 'Heal'.
gpxinspect.join_help: Appends another recording to this track — e.g. when the watch stopped mid-tour, or a multi-day trip comes as one file per day. Sensor data (heart rate, power …) stays with its own section.
gpxinspect.join_hint: Close the gap with “Heal → fill gaps with points”.
gpxinspect.join_shifted: Times of the appended track were shifted back (it overlapped).
gpxinspect.manual_help: Click two points on the map (A green, B red), then choose an action for the section between them.
gpxinspect.match_all_tip: Snap the WHOLE track onto the road network. Only useful for path/road-based tracks — for off-trail hikes it can distort the trace.
gpxinspect.match_all_warn: Caution: snaps the WHOLE track onto Mapbox roads and overwrites your recorded points — junctions can produce detours/loops. For gaps/outliers only, use “Heal”. Click again to confirm.
gpxinspect.match_hint: Only useful if the track follows paths/roads. Needs internet + Mapbox token.
gpxinspect.match_sel_hint: For a section that follows a path: set A and B, then let it find the route in between.
gpxinspect.match_sel_tip: Finds the actual road/path route between anchors A and B (Directions). Robust against GPS drift — no 50 m limit. Replaces the points in between with the route; time/elevation distributed. Undoable.
gpxinspect.mm_radius_tip: How far from a path a point still snaps. Small = only very close, large = catches more GPS drift but may snap to parallel roads. (Mapbox max 50 m.)
gpxinspect.points_help: A track is made up of many individual measurements — one for every time your device recorded its position. One point every 1–10 seconds is normal, so a long tour quickly adds up to several thousand. On the map each point is a small circle you can click. More points is not better: healing removes outliers and fills gaps, which changes the number.
gpxinspect.profil_geraten: “{art}” estimated from this tour’s speed (median {v} km/h) — you can change it.
gpxinspect.profile_help: Straight line = direct line between the points. Hiking/cycling/driving = look up the real route on the path network (Mapbox, internet + token) so the track follows the paths. Plausibility brake: if the route found is longer than 2.5× the straight-line distance it is probably a detour via the wrong junction — the gap is then filled straight, and the message says how often that happened. Very large gaps (flights, over 300 km) always stay straight.
gpxinspect.profile_tip: For 'snap gaps' and 'snap track': which path network to use.
gpxinspect.reduce_fehlt: Please enter a target point count
gpxinspect.route_detour: The route found makes a big detour/loop — not applied. Use “Fill gap (straight line)” or “Draw & fill path”.
gpxinspect.route_nomatch: No route found — A or B is too far from a road.
gpxinspect.routegaps_help: Instead of a straight line, find the real route on the path network (Mapbox, needs internet + token). Very large gaps like flights stay straight.
gpxinspect.routing: Finding a route between A and B …
gpxinspect.sel_a: Anchor A set — drag the point to move it · Delete to remove · click anchor B for a range.
gpxinspect.sel_klick_a: Click point A on the map, then point B — the stretch between them is healed.
gpxinspect.sens_help: How strict the search is. Low = only big outliers and large gaps, high = also small ones.
gpxinspect.sens_tip: How sensitively outliers are detected. Low = only big jumps, high = even small spikes. The marking updates live as you drag.
gpxinspect.snap_help: Snaps the whole track onto the path network via map matching. Only useful if the track really follows paths/roads.
gpxinspect.speed_fehlt: Please enter a speed in km/h
gpxinspect.speed_help: This track has no timestamps — typical for a planned route. Give it a desired speed and it gets a plausible time axis: duration, average speed and the time readouts in the animator work afterwards, and in a swarm it can run in “real clock time” mode. Recorded tracks don't need this — their broken timestamps are fixed precisely by “even out impossible speed” during auto-healing. And what this does NOT do: the length of the finished video is set in the animator (duration and pace of the camera run) — this button only changes the timestamps in the track.
gpxinspect.speedcolor_help: Colours the track by the speed between points: green = normal, yellow = brisk, orange = very fast, red = likely outlier. GPS jumps stand out immediately — then heal or smooth the section manually. Needs timestamps.
gpxinspect.speedthr_help: The speed from which a piece counts as an outlier (red). Empty = automatic, taken from this tour itself (green up to its usual speed, red only well above) — that works for hiking as well as driving. Enter a number and it applies as given: green up to a third, yellow up to two thirds, orange up to the threshold, red above it.
gpxinspect.tempo_cap_help: Empty = automatic (from the tour's median pace). Enter e.g. 15 if you know you were never faster than 15 km/h — anything above gets re-timed on healing.
gpxinspect.tools_help: Shrink the file's point count (real points are kept, chosen evenly along the distance) or rewrite the timestamps to a desired average speed — e.g. to animate a planned route at a realistic pace. Both only reach a file when you save.
gpxinspect.trim_after_tip: Remove everything after this point — this point becomes the new end (e.g. cut off a recording you forgot to stop at the end of the tour).
gpxinspect.trim_before_tip: Remove the start of the track up to this point — this point becomes the new start (e.g. cut off the drive in or standing still at the beginning).
gpxinspect.uebernehmen_pruefen: The tour changed by roughly %p % — please check keyframes and signs.
gpxinspect.uebernehmen_sicher: The old tour stays untouched — you can always open the original file again.
gpxinspect.uebernehmen_text: To the program the healed track is a new tour — your projects still belong to the old file. Should the animator, tour map, geotagger and elevation animator come along, including photos and signs?
gpxinspect.uebernehmen_titel: Carry your work over to the healed track?
gpxinspect.uebernehmen_vorbehalt: Depending on how much was healed, the transfer may not fit everywhere: keyframes, signs and photo pins sit at a position along the track. If only single outliers were smoothed you won't notice a thing. If a lot was inserted or cut away, they can shift — please take a quick look in that case.

quickstart.animator.intro: Turns your GPX into a cinematic video: the camera flies over the 3D map and traces the route.
quickstart.animator.step1: Load a track: Click “Choose track …” at the top or drag a GPX/FIT/TCX file straight into the window.
quickstart.animator.step2: Set the look: Pick map style, track colour and camera (pitch, rotation) in the sidebar. “Preview run” at the bottom shows the flight right away.
quickstart.animator.step3: Render: Choose resolution/FPS in the video settings at the very bottom and render the video.
quickstart.animator.tip: The animator starts on the world view (globe) as a cinema intro. “To start” or the preview run jumps to your track.
quickstart.animator.title: Animator — your track as a video
quickstart.geotagger.intro: Writes GPS coordinates (and optionally addresses) into your photos — based on your tour's GPX track and the capture time.
quickstart.geotagger.step1: Load track + photos: Load the tour's GPX, then “Select photos …” or drop a whole folder.
quickstart.geotagger.step2: Align the time: If the camera clock is off, correct it with the offset slider — the pins move live to the right spot.
quickstart.geotagger.step3: Write: Optionally “Fetch addresses”, then write the GPS data into the photos. The original stays untouched.
quickstart.geotagger.tip: Photos without track time can be placed by hand via “Snap to track” or dragging.
quickstart.geotagger.title: Geotagger — tag photos with GPS
quickstart.gpxinspect.intro: Repairs noisy tracks point by point: smooth outliers, fill gaps, cut sections, join several recordings into one track.
quickstart.gpxinspect.step1: Load a track: Choose a GPX at the top — every single point becomes visible.
quickstart.gpxinspect.step2: Heal: “Heal (automatic)” smooths outliers and fills gaps. For finer control use anchors A→B.
quickstart.gpxinspect.step3: Save: Save the healed track as GPX or TCX — the original is kept.
quickstart.gpxinspect.tip: “Join tracks” appends a second recording — handy when the watch stopped mid-tour.
quickstart.gpxinspect.title: GPX inspector — heal your track
quickstart.heightanim.intro: Animates a data curve of your track — elevation, heart rate, speed, cadence — building up live. With a transparent background it becomes a video overlay.
quickstart.heightanim.step1: Load a track: Load a GPX/FIT with the data you want (e.g. elevation or heart rate).
quickstart.heightanim.step2: Choose the series: Set the left axis at the top (e.g. elevation) and optionally a second series for the right axis (e.g. heart rate).
quickstart.heightanim.step3: Style + render: Set colours, lines, axes and render as a video — with alpha for the compositing track.
quickstart.heightanim.tip: For an overlay in your editing app, set background opacity to 0 and render as ProRes with alpha.
quickstart.heightanim.title: Data animator — sensor data as a video
quickstart.library.intro: Scans your track folders and shows every tour with image, date and numbers. Instead of guessing file names you search and filter — and hand a tour on with one click.
quickstart.library.step1: Add folders: Top right “Folders & scan” → “+ Add folder” and pick where your tracks live. Subfolders are included; 700 files take about 20 seconds.
quickstart.library.step2: Find again: Search box, year, activity, sorting in the bar above the tours — and three views: tiles, list, or a map with all tours at once.
quickstart.library.step3: Keep working: Click a tour and hand it to the animator, tour map, geotagger & co. on the right. A double-click sends it straight to the animator.
quickstart.library.tip: Under “Folders & scan”, “Fetch map images” puts a real map behind every tour — loaded once, then offline. Your files are never moved or deleted.
quickstart.library.title: Library — all tours in one place
quickstart.reiseroute.intro: Animates the journey to your tour: a route is computed from start and destination and flown like a track.
quickstart.reiseroute.step1: Set the stops: Type start and destination as addresses — or enable “click mode” and tap the map. Add as many waypoints as you like.
quickstart.reiseroute.step2: Choose the mode: Car, on foot or bicycle — this decides which ways the route takes.
quickstart.reiseroute.step3: “Compute route”: The route is built and can be flown and rendered just like in the animator.
quickstart.reiseroute.tip: “Flight route” instead of “follow roads” draws a direct line — good for flights or long distances.
quickstart.reiseroute.title: Travel route — animate the journey
quickstart.title: Quick start
quickstart.tourmap.intro: Creates a high-resolution still of your tour — perfect for thumbnails, your blog or as an overview.
quickstart.tourmap.step1: Load a track: Choose or drop a GPX at the top.
quickstart.tourmap.step2: Design the image: Map style, track look, start/end pins and the stats box (distance, climb …) — all WYSIWYG in the preview.
quickstart.tourmap.step3: “Render map as PNG”: Save the finished image at the resolution you want.
quickstart.tourmap.tip: What you see in the preview is exactly what ends up in the image — just drag the view into place.
quickstart.tourmap.title: Tour map — a static map PNG
quickstart.webkarte.intro: Exports a light, interactive map (Leaflet) to embed in your blog — visitors can zoom and tap the labels.
quickstart.webkarte.step1: Load a track: Choose a GPX at the top. Add more legs via “Add track”.
quickstart.webkarte.step2: Design: Track colour/width, map style (e.g. OpenStreetMap) and labels placed right on the map.
quickstart.webkarte.step3: Export: Export as HTML and embed it in your blog — optionally with a GDPR consent button.
quickstart.webkarte.tip: The preview here is exactly the export — no surprises when embedding.
quickstart.webkarte.title: Web map — an interactive map for the web

settings.maps.help.default: This style applies to every new project. Existing projects keep theirs; change it any time in the Animator or Tour Map. If a style's key is missing or the track lies outside the coverage, the app quietly falls back and tells you below the style field — it never aborts.
settings.maps.help.frei1: "Satellite (free)" uses the official aerial imagery of the national mapping agencies — often sharper than Mapbox (20–50 cm ground resolution). The app picks the source from your track's location, nothing to set up. Included: 15 German states (Hamburg missing), Austria, Switzerland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, France, Spain incl. the Canaries, Portugal, Italy, Czechia, Poland, Estonia, Japan and the USA.
settings.maps.help.frei2: If the track lies outside this coverage (e.g. Scandinavia, the UK, Canada), the app falls back to the OpenFreeMap map with terrain — use MapTiler for satellite there. At German state borders the neighbouring states are stacked so no strip stays empty.
settings.maps.help.frei3: OpenFreeMap (Liberty, Bright, Positron) are vector maps from OpenStreetMap data — free, no key, no limit, commercial use allowed. OpenStreetMap, OpenTopoMap, CyclOSM and Humanitarian are tile maps run by volunteers: free, but please don't render in bulk; the cache helps.
settings.maps.help.frei4: For all free sources: videos may be published, monetised too. The condition is the attribution in the picture, which the app sets automatically — please don't crop it away.
settings.maps.help.gelaende: 3D terrain works with every source: Mapbox styles use Mapbox terrain, MapTiler styles MapTiler's, all free styles the AWS terrain model (Mapzen). The terrain is tied to the style — a video without Mapbox contains no Mapbox data.
settings.maps.help.mapbox1: Mapbox was the app's only map source for a long time: satellite in 3D, streets, outdoors, light and dark. The styles stay — with your own token (free; since mid-2026 with a credit card at signup; nothing is charged within the free tier of 50,000 map loads per month).
settings.maps.help.mapbox2: The catch is in the fine print: Mapbox permits publishing videos with its map content only with purchased video rights (Product Terms §1.7 "Print or Video Use"). You may watch them privately; not on YouTube, Instagram or your website without buying rights. The app therefore blocks nothing but reminds you once per session before a video render with a Mapbox style.
settings.maps.help.mapbox3: Getting the token: create an account at account.mapbox.com, click the confirmation e-mail, open "Access tokens" in the dashboard, copy the "Default public token" (starts with pk.eyJ…) and paste it below. Public tokens are not secret, but don't hand them out anyway.
settings.maps.help.maptiler1: MapTiler provides satellite imagery and terrain for the whole world from one source — the complement where no official aerial imagery exists. The key is free, no credit card, three minutes: create an account at cloud.maptiler.com, click the confirmation e-mail, open "API Keys" on the left, copy the existing key and paste it below.
settings.maps.help.maptiler2: Important: leave the key's "Allowed HTTP origins" field empty. If you enter a website there, MapTiler locks out the render, which runs without a browser address — the preview would work, the video would stay black.
settings.maps.help.maptiler3: Free plan: 100,000 tile requests per month, enough for many renders — but non-commercial use only. A monetised channel needs the Flex plan (about $30/month). Videos for channels up to 100,000 subscribers are allowed under MapTiler Cloud Terms §5; above that, ask MapTiler first.
settings.maps.help.speicher1: The tile cache keeps downloaded map tiles on disk (in the app support folder). Preview and render share it: the second render of the same area is noticeably faster, and the servers of the mapping agencies and OpenStreetMap are spared — their terms even require such a cache. Mapbox tiles are not stored.
settings.maps.help.speicher2: The size is an upper limit: when the cache is full, the oldest tiles go first. 2 GB is a good value; 0 turns it off. "Clear" helps when an area has been re-flown and you want to see the fresh imagery.
settings.maps.help.test: Testing only: "force OSM" runs the app as if there were no Mapbox token — Mapbox styles then fall back to "Satellite (free)". The token stays saved. This shows you what a user without a token gets.
settings.maps.help.ueberblick1: Every map in the app — Animator, Tour Map, Inspector, Geotagger, Archive, Web Map — offers the same style list. It comes in three groups: free (video allowed), MapTiler (your own key) and Mapbox (video only with purchased rights). Each entry carries its badge, so there is nothing to remember.
settings.maps.help.ueberblick2: Why all this: Mapbox permits publishing videos containing its map content only if you have purchased video rights (Product Terms §1.7). For YouTube, Instagram etc. the free styles or MapTiler are the right choice — the source attribution is placed automatically at the bottom right of the picture and is part of the video.

signs.accent_hint: Colour of the speech-bubble tip or pin — independent of the background. “Auto” keeps the old behaviour.
signs.apply_all_hint: Apply appearance (shape/colors/font/shadow/size) AND behavior (timing/entry/zoom/show-whole-time) to all others — text/image/position/visibility stay
signs.bg_none_hint: No background (transparent) — e.g. image without a colored frame
signs.callout_dir_hint: Speech bubble only: which way the tip points at the location.
signs.deco_len_hint: Length of the posts for banner / signpost
signs.direction_hint: Signpost only: which way the arrow points.
signs.help: Signs and photos along the route — a photo is a sign with an image. With “📷 Add photos”, photos (with GPS) land automatically at their capture coordinates. Everything appears in the video as the marker reaches its point. In the list: ⠿ drag to reorder, checkbox = on/off, ✎ = edit, ✕ = delete.
signs.hint: Text signs along the route. They appear in the video as soon as the marker reaches the spot.
signs.list_hint: Click a sign (list or map) to open its settings.
signs.minWidth_hint: 0 = fits the text. Above 0 gives the sign a fixed minimum width — only then do left/center/right visibly move the text.
signs.move_active: Click on the track to move the sign … (Esc cancels)
signs.move_active_free: Click anywhere on the map to move the sign … (Esc cancels)
signs.move_armed: ↔ Now drag the sign on the map to where you want it.
signs.move_hint: ↔ To move a sign, just drag it on the map to where you want it.
signs.move_toast_free: 📍 Click the map for the new position — Esc cancels
signs.move_toast_track: 📍 Click the track for the new position — Esc cancels
signs.place_active: Click on the track to place the sign … (Esc cancels)
signs.place_active_free: Click anywhere on the map (e.g. a sight) … (Esc cancels)
signs.preview_all_hint: Preview only (for placing) — in the video they still appear per timing.
signs.shadow_dir_hint: ↘ Shadow direction is global — set it under Track → “Shadow direction” (applies to the track + all signs).
signs.tailpos_hint: Where the pointer sits along the edge. Moving it helps when the tip would cover the track.
signs.time_anchor_hint: For out-and-back routes: move the scrubber to the desired moment, then pin it here (resolves the same-place ambiguity).
signs.zoomScale_hint: If the sign grows while you zoom, its text is drawn at a slightly different size every frame — that makes the letters visibly shimmer. Off = calm, crisp text.
topbar.project.del_msg: Really delete „{name}"? The last remaining project will automatically be restored as „Standard".
topbar.project.no_session: Load a GPX to use projects.
tourmap.cam_taken: View taken over from the Animator. Reset with ⤢ (Fit to track).
tourmap.html.consent_default: To display the interactive map, map tiles are loaded from OpenStreetMap. Your IP address is transmitted to the map provider. By clicking “Load map” you agree to this.
tourmap.html.consent_hint: The map loads external OSM tiles only after a click — GDPR-friendly. Text is freely editable.
tourmap.html.modal_open_hint: Use “Open in browser” to view — double-clicking the file may only open an editor on some systems.
tourmap.html.section_hint: Exports the map exactly as previewed (route, signs, photos) as an interactive Leaflet map to embed in your blog.
tourmap.html.snippet_hint: Snippet to paste directly into a “Custom HTML” block:
tourmap.html.snippet_wp: In WordPress: insert a “Custom HTML” block and paste the snippet.
tourmap.html2.intro: Lightweight interactive map for your blog (Leaflet + OpenStreetMap). Just route + signs — deliberately minimal. The preview here is exactly the export.
tourmap.stats.empty_hint: Load a GPX file — track stats will appear here
tourmap.style.export_hint: The interactive HTML export only knows tile styles (OpenStreetMap, free satellite). For vector styles it uses OpenStreetMap; the PNG uses the chosen style.
tourmap.style.osm_disabled_body: Tour maps require a Mapbox token (for satellite & 3D). Rendering is disabled in OSM mode.
tourmap.style.osm_hint: OSM styles are token-free and carried over 1:1 into the interactive HTML export (WYSIWYG). Mapbox styles apply to the PNG export only.
webkarte.attribution: Embed “made with GPS Studio by reisezoom.com” link
webkarte.consent_preview_hint: Shows a blurred still of your map behind the consent text (embedded locally, GDPR-compliant). Off = much faster export, but an empty gate.
webkarte.export_rendering: Rendering the map – the preview image can take a few seconds …
webkarte.intro: Lightweight interactive map for the web. The track comes automatically from the GPX; place labels directly on the map. The preview here is exactly the export.
webkarte.labels_hint: Click “Add”, then tap the map. Drag to move, click to rename/delete.
webkarte.leaflet_hint_cdn: Loads Leaflet from the public unpkg CDN (smallest file). With the GDPR button on, only after “Load map”.
webkarte.leaflet_hint_inline: Leaflet is written fully into the HTML – no external request (GDPR-clean, works offline), the file grows ~160 KB.
webkarte.leaflet_hint_url: Loads leaflet.css + leaflet.js from your base URL (you host the two files yourself).
webkarte.tracks_hint: The first track comes from the loaded GPX. Add further stages or tours here — each with its own colour, width, name and start/finish pins.
